title: Cloud Connector on AWS: CloudFormation templates, order, and parameter defaults
aliases: cloud connector add-on template private access route 53

prose.text: Zscaler's CloudFormation templates deploy Cloud Connector into a VPC the customer already has. The Terraform path is in [[cloud-connector.aws.reference-modules]]. {{template-version}} {{china-govcloud}}

prose.label: Autoscaling template.
prose.text: {{asg-prerequisites}} {{asg-defaults}} {{asg-recommendations}} How the group then scales is in [[cloud-connector.aws.autoscaling]].

prose.label: Private Access add-on.
prose.text: {{zpa-addon}} {{zpa-addon-params}} {{zpa-addon-rules}} Help and the template disagree on the inputs {{divergence:zpa-addon-inputs}}.

checks.do: Whether the Pre-Deployment Template stack exists and is current before the starter template was deployed.
Whether the workload route table was edited after the stack completed.
Whether the HTTP Monitor Probe Port parameter was set.
For autoscaling, whether the Lambda ZIP is in an S3 bucket in the deployment region and the template was left at one autoscaling group per availability zone.
For the Private Access add-on, whether the routes from the resolver endpoint subnets to the target IPs go via Cloud Connector, and whether the inputs match the deployed template rather than Help.
Whether the GWLB add-on was layered onto an autoscaling stack, which already contains a Gateway Load Balancer.

existing-vpc.statement: The CloudFormation templates create the resources to deploy and operate Cloud Connector in an existing VPC.

quotes: Use the templates in the CloudFormation repository to create the deployment resources you need to deploy and operate Cloud Connector in an existing virtual private cloud (VPC).

template-sets.statement: A standard deployment (no autoscaling) uses the Pre-Deployment Template, the Starter Deployment Template, and optionally the GWLB add-on and the Private Access add-on; an advanced (autoscaling) deployment uses the Pre-Deployment Template, the Starter Deployment Template with Autoscaling and GWLB, and optionally the Private Access add-on.

quotes: | Standard Deployment (No Autoscaling) | Advanced Deployment (Autoscaling) |
| Pre-Deployment Template Starter Deployment Template Add-on Template with Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) (optional) (Optional) Add-on Template with Private Access (ZPA) |
Pre-Deployment Template Starter Deployment Template with Autoscaling and Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) Add-on Template with Private Access (optional) |

template-names.statement: The template files are zs_cc_cf_template_zscc_macro (Pre-Deployment), zs_cc_cf_template_simple (Starter), zs_cc_cf_template_zpa_r53 (Private Access add-on), zs_cc_cf_template_gwlb (GWLB add-on) and zs_cc_cf_template_asg_gwlb (Starter with Autoscaling and GWLB).

quotes: Use the Pre-Deployment Template (zs_cc_cf_template_zscc_macro)
Use the Starter Deployment Template (zs_cc_cf_template_simple)
Use the Add-on Template with Private Access (zs_cc_cf_template_zpa_r53)
Use the Add-on Template with GWLB (zs_cc_cf_template_gwlb)
Use the Starter Deployment Template with Autoscaling and GWLB (zs_cc_cf_template_asg_gwlb)

pre-deployment-first.statement: The Pre-Deployment Template stack must be deployed before any Cloud Connector CloudFormation deployment, and an out-of-date Pre-Deployment stack must be updated and replaced.

quotes: Before deploying your Cloud Connectors using CloudFormation, you must upload the Pre-Deployment Template to the AWS CloudFormation console and deploy the Pre-Deployment Template stack.
If there is an existing Pre-Deployment Template stack that is out of date, you must update and replace the existing template.

probe-port-required.statement: The HTTP Monitor Probe Port parameter must be defined to check the liveliness of the Cloud Connectors and to achieve high availability.

quotes: You must define the HTTP Monitor Probe Port parameter to check the liveliness of the designated Cloud Connectors and to achieve high availability.

standard-defaults.statement: In the Starter Deployment Template, EBS encryption, the Cloud Tag Collection IAM policy, and a management security group rule permitting egress TCP/12002 to Zscaler Support servers all default to true; Help says disabling the support rule is not recommended.

evidence.after: EBS Encryption Enabled: From the drop-down menu, select true to enable EBS encryption (default) or false to disable it.
quotes: select true to enable Cloud Tag Collection IAM Policy creation (default) or false to disable it.

select true to enable the creation of a Management Security Group rule that permits egress TCP/12002 Zscaler Support Server Destinations (default) or false to disable rule creation. (Disabling is not recommended

ha-addon-deprecated.statement: The Add-on Template with High Availability, which takes route tables with affinity for each Cloud Connector and a Lambda package from S3, is deprecated.

quotes: Add-on Template with High Availability (deprecated)
List of Route Tables with affinity for each Cloud Connector: Enter the route tables associated with each Cloud Connector.
S3 Key for Lambda Deployment Package: Enter the AWS S3 key for the Lambda deployment package ZIP file.

asg-prerequisites.statement: An autoscaling deployment needs a provisioning template with autoscaling Enabled, which Zscaler Support enables, and an S3 bucket in the deployment region holding the Zscaler Cloud Connector Lambda ZIP file, whose bucket name and key are stack parameters.

evidence.after: Create a stack in the AWS CloudFormation console with Autoscaling (Advanced Deployment).
quotes: Cloud Connector with autoscaling requires a new provisioning template with autoscaling set to Enabled. To enable autoscaling, contact Zscaler Support.
To deploy Cloud Connectors with autoscaling, you must first create a new Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) bucket and store your Lambda ZIP file.
Lambda S3 Bucket Name: Enter the name of the AWS S3 bucket in this region where the Lambda deployment package ZIP file exists.
Lambda S3 Key: Enter the Lambda S3 key.

asg-defaults.statement: In the autoscaling template, availability-zone-based autoscaling groups default to true (one group per zone), the secret name defaults to ZS/CC/credentials, the instance size is small with other sizes not yet supported for autoscaling, and leaving the AMI blank deploys the latest Marketplace AMI.

quotes: select true to create one autoscaling group for each availability zone (default) or false to create a single autoscaling group spanning all selected availability zones.
By default, the name is set to ZS/CC/credentials.
Zscaler Cloud Connector Instance Size: By default, this field is set to small. Other sizes are not yet supported for autoscaling.
Leave blank to deploy the latest marketplace AMI (recommended).

asg-recommendations.statement: For the autoscaling template Zscaler recommends a target CPU value of 80%, warm pool instances in the Stopped state to reduce cost, and 5-tuple flow stickiness; the tag-collection policy setting applies only when CloudFormation creates a new IAM role.

quotes: enter a target value number (recommended default 80%)
Zscaler recommends selecting Stopped to reduce cost.
Zscaler recommends selecting 5-tuple for optimal load disbursement unless otherwise required for your specific environments.
select true to enable Cloud Tag Collection IAM Policy creation (default) or false to disable it. This setting is enforced only if CloudFormation creates a new IAM Role.

zpa-addon.statement: The Private Access add-on creates an outbound Route 53 resolver and up to 10 resolver rules, one per domain, takes the Cloud Connector's service ENI, and uses the Private Access cloud name ZPA for production clouds and ZPA-Beta for all others.

quotes: Outbound Route 53 resolver
Up to 10 Resolver rules, one per domain
For all production clouds, your Private Access cloud name is ZPA. For all other clouds, your Private Access cloud name is ZPA-Beta.
ServiceENI ID of Zscaler CC: Enter the elastic service interface (ENI) of the Zscaler Cloud Connector instance.
You can enter up to 10 domain names.

route-after-stack.statement: After the CloudFormation deployment, the route table and associated subnet must be modified so traffic from the private workload subnet goes to Cloud Connector; by default traffic leaves the workload subnet without it.

quotes: After you finish deploying the Cloud Connector from the AWS CloudFormation console, modify your route table and associated subnet to ensure that traffic is sent from the private workload subnet to Cloud Connector. By default, traffic is going out of the workload subnet.

monitoring-page.statement: A deployed Cloud Connector appears on the dashboard, and the Cloud & Branch Connector Monitoring page shows the name, group, location, geolocation and status of the deployed AMIs.

quotes: A deployed Cloud Connector is displayed on the dashboard. The Cloud & Branch Connector Monitoring page provides information on the name, group, location, geolocation (shown below), and status of the Cloud Connector AMIs deployed in your cloud account.

template-version.statement: The repository's CloudFormation templates are version 1.3.3, which its changelog dates 2024-08-30.

quotes: Description: Zscaler Cloud Connector Starter Deployment Template v1.3.3

macro-transform.statement: The Pre-Deployment Template creates a CloudFormation macro named ZSCC-Macro, and the Starter, GWLB add-on, Private Access add-on and autoscaling templates each call it as a transform with the operation ZSCCSIMPLE, ZSCCGWLB, ZSCCZPA or ZSCCASG respectively.

quotes: Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Macro
Name: 'ZSCC-Macro'
operation : ZSCCSIMPLE
operation : ZSCCGWLB
operation : ZSCCZPA
operation : ZSCCASG

macro-lookups.statement: When no AMI is given the macro finds the newest AWS Marketplace image by product code, using a separate product code in China regions, and it reads the Secrets Manager secret by name, ZS/CC/credentials unless the secret-name parameter says otherwise.

quotes: if RegionName.startswith('cn-'):
describe_images(Owners=["aws-marketplace"], Filters=filters)
key=lambda x: x.get("CreationDate")
ImageId = response[-1].get("ImageId")
SecretManagerSecretName = event["templateParameterValues"].get("ZscalerSecretManagerSecretName", "ZS/CC/credentials")
secret = secretsmanager_client.get_secret_value(SecretId=SecretManagerSecretName)
ImageId = event.get("templateParameterValues").get("ZscalerOsAmi") else: RegionName = boto3.session.Session().region_name
ImageCode = "axnpwhsb4facossmbm1h9yad6" else: ImageCode = event["fragment"]["Mappings"]["Product2Code"]["CloudConnector"]["Code"]
filters = [{"Name": "product-code", "Values":[ImageCode]}]

china-govcloud.statement: AWS GovCloud (US) support arrived in template version 1.1.0, and AWS China (Beijing) and (Ningxia) support through the China Marketplace in 1.3.3.

quotes: ## [1.1.0] - 2023-11-1 ------------ FEATURES: * AWS GovCloud (US) support
## 1.3.3 - 2024-08-30 ------------ ENHANCEMENTS: * add support for AWS China Marketpkace deployments in the AWS China (Beijing) region and AWS China (Ningxia) region

gwlb-addon-compat.statement: The GWLB add-on template is compatible only with the Starter Deployment Template, because autoscaling deployments include the Gateway Load Balancer automatically, and Zscaler's recommended deployment method is GWLB.

quotes: Zscaler's recommended deployment method is Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). This add-on is only compatible with Starter Deployment Template as Auto Scaling deployments include GWLB automatically.

simple-defaults.statement: In the Starter template the EC2 instance type defaults to m6i.large, the size to small and the HTTP monitor probe port to 50000 (allowed values 80 and 1024 to 65535), and the instance has an EBS-optimized gp3 volume on /dev/sda1.

quotes: Default: m6i.large
CCInstanceType: AllowedValues: - small - medium - large Default: small
Allowed values are 80, 1024-65535. Defaults to 50000
EbsOptimized: "true"
VolumeType: "gp3"
Description: Zscaler Cloud Connector Starter Deployment Template v1.3.3
BlockDeviceMappings: - DeviceName: "/dev/sda1" Ebs: VolumeType: "gp3"

zpa-addon-params.statement: The Private Access add-on takes up to 6 resolver endpoint subnets and up to 6 target IPs, requires that the routes from those subnets to the target IPs go via Cloud Connector, and defaults the target IPs to 185.46.212.88 and 185.46.212.89.

quotes: Subnets (max 6) for the Resolver Endpoints. The routes to reach the Target IPs from these subnets must be via Zscaler Cloud Connector(s)
Target IPs (max 6) for the Resolver Endpoints to forward DNS queries. The Target IPs must be reachable via Zscaler Cloud Connector(s).

zpa-addon-rules.statement: The Private Access add-on creates system-type resolver rules for the Zscaler cloud domain, the Private Access cloud domain (prod.zpath.net for ZPA, zpabeta.net for ZPA-Beta), zscaler.com, freebsd.org, ntp.org and amazonaws.com, plus a forwarding rule per application domain whose resolver security group allows all protocols in and out from 0.0.0.0/0.

quotes: DomainName: !Ref ZscalerCloudName Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ZSCloudRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
DomainName: !FindInMap [ZPACloudMap, !Ref ZPACloudName, domain] Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ZPACloudRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
ZPA: domain: prod.zpath.net ZPA-Beta: domain: zpabeta.net
DomainName: zscaler.com Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ZScalerComRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
DomainName: freebsd.org Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-FreeBSDRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
DomainName: ntp.org Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-NtpOrgCloudRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
DomainName: amazonaws.com Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AmazonAWSRule' RuleType: SYSTEM
SecurityGroupIngress: - IpProtocol: '-1' CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0 SecurityGroupEgress: - IpProtocol: '-1' CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
ResolverEndpointId: !Ref AppSegmentOutboundResolver RuleType: FORWARD

asg-input-validation.statement: The autoscaling template's macro checks that every Cloud Connector subnet is in the chosen VPC and in one of the chosen availability zones and that each chosen zone has a subnet, and VPC endpoint subnets, when given, override the Cloud Connector subnets with one picked per zone.

quotes: Subnet {ec2_subnet.get('SubnetId')} is not part of Vpc {vpc}.
is not part of given zones {availability_zones}.
does not have any subnets specified in Vpc Endpoint Subnets if specified or in CloudConnector Subnets
override the CC Subnets. One subnet in each AZ is picked
Description: Zscaler Cloud Connector Pre-Deployment Macro Template v1.3.3
[Optional] A List of comma-separated VPC EP Subnets to create VPC Endpoints in (one per Az). Specifying subnets here will override Cloud-connector subnets being used for VPC Endpoints
Description: Zscaler Cloud Connector Starter Deployment Template with Auto Scaling and GWLB v1.3.3

zpa-addon-inputs.summary: What the Private Access add-on takes as input: Help lists a Cloud Connector service ENI and up to 10 domain names, the template lists neither and bounds the domains by length.

positions.says: The add-on takes the Cloud Connector's service ENI and up to 10 domain names.

quotes: ServiceENI ID of Zscaler CC: Enter the elastic service interface (ENI) of the Zscaler Cloud Connector instance.
You can enter up to 10 domain names.

positions.says: The template's parameters are the Zscaler cloud name, ZPA cloud name, VPC, resolver endpoint subnets and target IPs, plus application domain names limited to 4096 characters; it has no service ENI parameter.

quotes: Parameters: - ZscalerCloudName - ZPACloudName - VPCID - ResolverEPSubnets - TargetIPs
Comma Seperated Application Domain Names (Max 4096 characters)

zpa-addon-inputs.impact: A deployment written from Help supplies a service ENI the current template does not ask for, and a domain list is bounded by 4096 characters in the template, not by a count of 10; read the template version actually deployed.
